questions.question: Which feature best distinguishes innate immunity from adaptive immunity?
choices: Innate immunity is rapid and pattern-based; adaptive immunity is antigen-specific and develops memory
Innate immunity is mediated only by antibodies
Adaptive immunity has no role in host defense
Innate immunity cannot respond to tissue injury
questions.explanation: Innate immunity provides rapid pattern-based defense; adaptive immunity is antigen-specific and generates immunologic memory. The systems cooperate.

questions.question: A patient has myocardial necrosis after coronary occlusion and develops inflammation without infection. What most directly initiates this innate response?
choices: Pathogen-associated molecular patterns from bacteria
Damage-associated molecular patterns released by injured host tissue
Loss of all cytokine signaling
Antibody memory alone
questions.explanation: Injured host cells release or expose DAMPs. Pattern-recognition receptors detect these danger signals and can activate inflammation without infection.

questions.question: Which complement function is correctly matched?
choices: C3b—opsonization; C5a—chemotaxis/inflammation; C5b-9—membrane attack complex
C3b—membrane attack complex; C5a—opsonization; C5b-9—fever
C3b—insulin release; C5a—antibody production; C5b-9—vasodilation only
C3b—T-cell memory; C5a—red-cell production; C5b-9—coagulation
questions.explanation: C3b coats pathogens for phagocytosis, C5a strongly promotes inflammatory-cell recruitment, and C5b-9 forms the pore-producing membrane attack complex.

questions.question: Why is an elevated CRP insufficient by itself to diagnose bacterial infection?
choices: CRP is produced only during viral illness
CRP is an acute-phase marker that can rise with infection or sterile inflammation
CRP always indicates sepsis
CRP measures complement deficiency
questions.explanation: CRP supports an inflammatory response but is nonspecific. Infection, ischemia, trauma, autoimmune disease, and other processes can elevate it.

questions.question: Which sequence best describes neutrophil movement into inflamed tissue?
choices: Margination → rolling → adhesion → diapedesis → chemotaxis
Chemotaxis → diapedesis → adhesion → rolling → margination
Adhesion → rolling → margination → chemotaxis → diapedesis
Diapedesis → chemotaxis → rolling → adhesion → margination
questions.explanation: The standard conceptual sequence is margination, rolling, adhesion, diapedesis/transmigration, then chemotaxis toward inflammatory signals.

questions.question: A patient has fever, leukocytosis, and tachycardia. What is the best FNP interpretation?
choices: These findings prove bacterial infection and mandate the same treatment for every patient
They are systemic inflammatory clues that require source assessment, severity evaluation, host-risk review, and a differential diagnosis
They rule out serious disease if blood pressure is normal once
They indicate adaptive immunity has failed
questions.explanation: Systemic findings are not a diagnosis. Integrate vital signs, mental status, perfusion, examination, source clues, and risk factors to determine urgency and cause.

questions.question: A patient receiving a C5 complement inhibitor develops abrupt fever, severe headache, vomiting, and petechial rash. What is the key clinical concern?
choices: Routine medication intolerance appropriate for delayed review
Invasive meningococcal disease requiring immediate emergency evaluation
Simple tension headache without infection risk
Cellulitis confined to the skin
questions.explanation: Complement inhibition increases meningococcal risk. This symptom pattern may represent invasive disease and requires immediate emergency evaluation and a clear medication handoff.

questions.question: Which local finding is explained most directly by increased vascular permeability during acute inflammation?
choices: Tissue edema from movement of protein-rich fluid into the interstitium
Loss of all local blood flow
Reduced tissue pressure
Immediate fibrosis
questions.explanation: Inflammatory mediators increase vascular permeability, allowing fluid and proteins to leave the circulation and produce edema.

questions.question: A 72-year-old has fever, productive cough, RR 30/min, BP 84/52, confusion, and cool extremities. Which is the safest FNP decision?
choices: Schedule routine outpatient follow-up after obtaining a CRP
Recognize possible sepsis with impaired perfusion and arrange emergency escalation
Treat only the cough and reassess next week
Assume findings are due to uncomplicated viral illness
questions.explanation: Hypotension, altered mental status, tachypnea, and poor perfusion with suspected infection are emergency findings. Prompt escalation is required.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between local infection and sepsis?
choices: Every local infection causes sepsis
Sepsis is a life-threatening dysregulated host response to infection that can impair perfusion and organ function
Sepsis can be ruled out by a single normal laboratory result
Sepsis is defined only by fever
questions.explanation: Sepsis is a life-threatening emergency involving a dysregulated host response to infection and organ dysfunction. It requires clinical assessment rather than reliance on one sign or test.
